speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you are experiencing hematuria and right flank pain. To begin my assessment, how would you describe the nature of the pain—is it constant, colicky, or sharp? Have you noticed any fever, chills, nausea, or changes in your urinary frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The combination of visible hematuria, right flank pain, and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections is highly suggestive of a renal calculus, potentially with associated infection.
